newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - SEPT 9.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - SEPT 9.

text.p: PRAVO - The chairman of the Civic Democratic Alliance, Jan Kalvoda, and the leader of the Christian Democratic Union - Czechoslovak People's Party (KDU-CSL), Josef Lux, announced their support for further economic liberalisation, especially for the deregulation of rent and energy prices. These parties are the junior partners in the ruling government coalition.

- The consolodation program for the banking sphere, begun in 1995, is complete and currently no bank is in a poor financial state according to the chief executive director of the Czech National Bank, Ota Kaftan. Kaftan was responding to a question on whether more banks could go bankrupt.
- Flooding in Trinecke Zelezarny, caused by incessant showers on Saturday, resulted in a decrease of 6000 tonnes of steel from expected production.
- President Vaclav Havel agreed that foreign specialists should be asked to help in the investigation of the Kreditni Banka bankruptcy.

- It is possible that the supervisory council of Ceska Pojistovna will agree to the sale of 16 percent of the insurance institution to the PPF investment group from Investicni a Postovni Banka. This is in spite of the fact that the National Property Fund, which owns 26 percent of Ceska Pojistovna, disagrees with the sale.
- Skoda Plzen did not come to an agreement on Friday with Ceskoslovenska Obchodni Banka and Finop on the sale of Motokov, a Prague-based trading company.
HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - The PPF investment company intends to reveal its ownership structure during the course of this week.
- Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus, accompanied by more than 30 Czech businessmen, arrived in Malaysia yesterday. This is the second stop in Klaus's week-long tour of Asia and the Pacific Rim after Japan.
- The creation of a parliamentary commission to investigate the bankruptcy of Kreditni Banka could occur at the next meeting of parliament at the beginning of October.
- ABB company, which posts a yealy turnover of 30 billion dollars (795.57 billion crowns) has opened a new branch office in Ostrava
